content: A maculopapular rash is characterized by a flat, red area on the skin that is interspersed with small, raised bumps. These bumps, known as papules, are small, elevated lesions, while the flat, discolored areas are referred to as macules. Together, they form the distinctive appearance of this type of rash. The rash may resemble the spots or bumps seen in conditions such as measles. It is also commonly observed in patients with scarlet fever. Additionally, this type of rash can occur as a side effect of consuming high doses of niacin or no-flush niacin, typically in the range of 2000 to 2500 mg, which is sometimes used in the treatment of low HDL cholesterol levels.
